summary: A combined CDF fire station and lookout in Kings County, staffed into the 1980s and closed; sources disagree on when the building went up.

facts.design: CDF Plan 804 combined fire station and lookout, with a 10,000-gallon concrete water tank
facts.status_note: Abandoned and partly open to the elements; the station closed in 1986.

access.note: Abandoned; no public use is documented. Do not enter the building.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register's 1953 date does not match the Fresno-Kings unit history (early 1940s) or a December 1952 photo caption that already shows the station. The 1935-1941 'Cottonwood Pass' lookout reported by the California Lookouts page may have been a predecessor on the same ridge, but the sources read do not confirm that it was the same building.

notes_for_editor: Build date is the main dispute (Register 1953; unit history early 1940s; archive caption December 1952). The 1935-1941 lookout at the pass may be a predecessor station rather than the same building. The 1976 and 1985 items rest on former firefighters' recollections printed on the Register page. A Facebook group comment (not used, social media) says the land was sold in the 2000s; ownership is unverified. The 'closed' access level reflects abandonment and the 1986 closure, not a posted notice. Kings County per Register. The Fresno-Kings unit history says the site overlooked Sun Valley, while the 1935 item says it overlooked the Kettleman Plains; the story keeps the 1935 wording, which is footnoted to that item.
